title: Peninsula Indivisible Wednesday Rally
description:
Please join Peninsula Indivisible for our rally in Newport News, VA. 

It’s going to be hot, hot, hot, so please bring water, wear sunscreen, take care of yourself.

Thank you for joining us. As a member of our community, you commit to keeping our events peaceful, being respectful, creating a safe environment, and taking personal responsibility for your behavior. Our rallies are expected to be peaceful, safe and representative of our worldview. We will not engage in hateful, angry or mean gestures, language or signs.

Please do not engage with counter-protesters. Just smile and then ignore them.

Please do not return angry gestures or language with vehicular traffic. Just smile and wave.

We’ll refine our Code of Conduct as we go on. For now, when in doubt, please err on the side of kindness.

In the words of Michele Obama, “When they go low, we go high”.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

title: 12 Days to Democracy Lands in DC! Reading the Letters of Farcie.
description:
Call or text 773-234-1280 for up-to-date information.

Tomorrow, Saturday, June 28th, we will complete our journey as we arrive in Washington, DC. Our ETA is between 2 and 3 PM in Lafayette Park. "The '12 Days to Democracy' may conclude, but the spirit ignited within these days burns brighter than ever. We've shown that celebrating community and standing for justice are inseparable, and that 'we, the people,' through our collective dissent, are the true architects of a more just world. This is not an end, but a powerful beginning," Judy says, with pride, about a movement that she only dreamed about in April 2025.

The "12 Days to Democracy" invites individuals to join in this journey of action and reflection, exploring how we can create a democracy that is transparent, equitable, and truly serves everyone.

For more information about the "12 Days to Democracy" march, including how to participate, support the effort, view the detailed itinerary, and delve deeper into its vision for a re-energized democracy, please visit http://www.democracy12.com.

title: Chuck the Clock — It’s Time for a Record-Breaking Vote-a-Rama!
description:
The Senate vote on the MAGA Murder Budget is imminent—and it’s time for Chuck to lead a Vote-a-Rama for the history books.

A vote-a-rama is a marathon Senate session where senators vote on a rapid-fire series of amendments—often dozens or even hundreds—usually tied to budget bills. It can go all night. There’s no cap on the number of amendments, which makes it a powerful tool to delay bad legislation, force tough votes, and shine a spotlight on what’s at stake. It’s procedural chaos—by design.

The longest vote-a-rama on record happened on March 13, 2008, with 44 roll-call votes over more than 10 hours. That’s the bar. Chuck can beat it.

The devastation buried in the BBB (Big Bad Bill) will harm millions of Americans. Every hour Democrats can delay this vote is an hour more for the public to learn what’s inside—and demand their Senators and Congressmembers stop it.

Join us, NY Communities for Change, and Food and Water Watch Saturday morning outside Chuck’s building to stiffen his spine, fuel his resolve, and make it clear:

He must use every tool—including a record-breaking vote-a-rama—to grind this bill to a halt.

title: Good Trouble Lives On in Dripping Springs!
description:
John Lewis, Congressman and Civil Rights Leader, championed engaging in GOOD TROUBLE, and in honor of him, we plan to have a PARADE around Dripping Springs.  We will be flying our American flags, tarting up our cars, trucks and motorcycles and showing our opposition to Trump and Company's UNconstitutional abuses and excesses.  

Our rights, and the future of our democracy are at stake, and we will not   remain silent.  Stand up and make your voices heard! Make Good Trouble!

We plan to have some fun while we exercise our First Amendment Right to Free Speech and Freedom of Assembly.

We shall meet on  Saturday, July 19th, 10 am at the  City Hall parking lot in Dripping Springs, at 511 Mercer Street.  

Instead of our traditional street corner protest at RR 12 and Hwy 290, we thought y'all would enjoy taking a little ride around the neighborhood, ending up for lunch at El Rey.

Bring signs, flags, shoe polish, bunting, pretty much anything you think might look great on (and not fall off) your vehicle.  Be fancy, dress up if you want, and Let's Ride for Democracy!

We will meet this time, not at Veterans Park (the DS Farmer's Market is there that Saturday), but right down Mercer Street at the DS City Hall parking lot.  It might be good to do any elaborate decorating before you show up, but we will also be working on our cars while we gather.

This is our way of letting our friends and neighbors know what we stand for, and what we will not fall for. 

Like always, our event will be peaceful, law-abiding, non-confrontational and non-violent.  We encourage everyone to de-escalate any unpleasant interactions with the public.  Smile and wave, even at those giving you the finger, or honking aggressively. 

We also ask that you leave all weapons at home, and do not intentionally offend the public by displaying profanity or vulgar words on signs or flags.

In light of recent events, our movement has evolved to include Anti-War sentiment, and slogans.  Peace and Justice at home, and abroad, is our goal.  

The nationwide "Good Trouble Lives On" events are mostly going to be held on Thursday, July 17th, the anniversary of John Lewis's passing, but upon reflection, we thought our crowd might prefer continuing our Saturday morning tradition.  So, we are meeting on Saturday, not Thursday, as that just seemed more our style.

Remember: We meet EVERY Saturday morning, at 10 am, usually at Veterans Park, and then walk on over to the intersection with our signs and flags, our smiles and waves. 

Call 512-829-1626 if you have any question as to whether bad weather or other contingencies may require us to move or cancel our protest.

title: Neighborhood Door-Knocking for Democrats!
description:
**We're hitting the doors this summer to let voters know about the important local and statewide elections happening this year!**

Odd year elections are just as important as even year elections, but they don't get the same amount of attention. Let's try to fix that! It's up to us to inform local Dems about the critical judicial elections and retentions on our ballots this year, as well as the municipal races and school board seats that impact our lives and our communities every day. 


**WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW**

**If you've never canvassed before, we will train you!** Canvassing is a fun, easy way to get to know your neighbors and have a HUGE local impact. 

**If you HAVE canvassed before, we'll still train you!** We'll go over the ins ^ outs of what's on the ballot this time around, and help you inform voters to prepare them to vote this year.

**We'll be using MiniVAN to canvass, which is an app that helps you automatically record the information from your conversations.** MiniVAN does require a smartphone, so if you haven't used MiniVAN yet, download the app from your app store before your canvassing shift so we can get you all set up and ready to knock. 

**We're knocking on Democratic doors!** These should be friendly conversations to let folks know about what's on their ballot this year. 

If you have any questions, please let us know. Canvassing is a perfect way to make local voters feel heard, while giving them vital info that they need to both cast their own ballots and spread the word to their friends and neighbors about why voting is so important in 2025!

**Our 2025 canvassing will start on July 20th!** We'll be canvassing on Sundays for now, and will add days and shifts as we head into the fall. Please note that we will NOT be canvassing on Sunday, August 10th (that's the date of our Dems for Democracy Summer Picnic at Columbia Park - hope to see you there instead!) or on Sunday, August 31st (Labor Day Weekend).
